Advitiix Management Tool — Portfolio Case Study

One connected tool for 4 roles: replacing email, chats, and spreadsheets.

Advitiix Management Tool is one connected internal system with four role-based apps: Employee, Project Manager, Admin / HR, and Receptionist (Food Tracker). They share one design system, one modular shell, and one set of business rules.

{/* Meta Grid */}

Role

Sole Product Designer & Dev

Company

Advitiix Technovate (~25 staff)

Scope

4 Role Apps (0-to-1)

Ownership

UX, IA, Copy & Coded UI

{/* Hero Interactive Role Wireframe */}
{/* Section 01: The Problem & Research Discovery */}
01 Context & Problem

Information was scattered across chat, email, and memory.

Day-to-day operations ran through WhatsApp messages, informal emails, and direct DMs to HR. Simple employee questions—like remaining leave, pending request approvals, or daily lunch counts—required interrupting HR or searching through old threads.

Managers approved requests casually in chat without seeing project impact. HR maintained leave balances manually in spreadsheets, causing numbers to drift. Reception had no reliable daily meal headcount, leading to daily food waste and disputed month-end bills.

The Goal: Build one trusted single source of truth for leave, attendance, tasks, food, and inventory with role-based depth—keeping employees simple while giving Admin the required control.

{/* Section 02: The 4 Role-Based Apps Breakdown */}
02 The 4 Role-Based Apps

One shell. Different depth for each role.

All four apps share the same navigation order: Dashboard, Attendance, Leave Management, Projects & Tasks, Food, and Inventory.

{/* Section 04: Design Principles & Key Learnings */}
04 Key Takeaways

Reflections from building from 0 to 1.

01

Write business rules before screens

Defining things like "what counts as overdue" or "when is a bill settled" removed most design debates before drawing a single rectangle.

02

Separate facts that look related

Attendance is not working on a task. Being absent does not mean no meal was ordered. Keeping these signals uncoupled prevented the most common user confusion.

03

Design for 4 roles with 1 system

A shared shell and unified design tokens allowed the PM, Admin, and Receptionist tools to be prototyped and coded rapidly once the Employee core patterns were tested.

04

One place instead of three channels

Advitiix staff now rely on one trusted dashboard instead of jumping between WhatsApp threads, emails, and manual follow-ups to HR.
